Exploit that each side of both `Iff`s is independently true, so prove the conjunction componentwise and construct each equivalence by ignoring the hypothesis from the opposite side.

- First equivalence:
  - Transfer Hausdorffness by restriction of scalars. From `Ideal.map (algebraMap R S) I ≤ J`, obtain
    \[
    I^n\!\cdot M \subseteq J^n\!\cdot M
    \]
    for every `n`; the scalar-tower assumption identifies the relevant `R`- and `S`-actions. Hence `J`-adic Hausdorffness implies `I`-adic Hausdorffness.
  - The other statement is the defining characterization of `AdicCompletion.IsAdicCauchy`: consecutive terms are congruent modulo `I^n • ⊤`.

- Second equivalence:
  - For the Hausdorff statement, turn each `SModEq (I^n • ⊤) x 0` into membership `x ∈ I^n • ⊤`. Thus `x` lies in the intersection of all these submodules, which is `⊥` by `IsHausdorff`, so `x = 0`.
  - Pointwise equality of two `AdicCauchySequence`s gives equality of their underlying functions by function extensionality, then equality of the subtypes by `Subtype.ext`.

The essential ingredients are the ideal inclusion plus scalar-tower compatibility for the first transfer; everything else is definitional unfolding, intersection membership, and extensionality.
